subject: Surge overlay pricing & sizing options for Acme Analytics Dedicated pool
messages:
From: Sarah Liao <sarah.liao@acme-analytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme-analytics.com>, Acme Analytics - Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Q4 event - temporary spike needs + Dedicated sizing question

Hey Jordan,

Quick background: we expect a one-week, predictable spike for our Q4 product launch (estimated 6x baseline) and are leaning toward Redwood Dedicated. We love the predictability of reserved commits, but we need an overlay option so we don't over-commit capacity for the rest of the quarter.

Can you share: 1) recommended GPU pool sizing approach (steady commit vs. commit + overlay), 2) how surge/overlay pricing is structured (cooldowns, max surge rate, per-minute billing), and 3) any commitment discount tradeoffs if we add a small monthly reserved bump to reduce overlay cost?

I've attached our monthly usage preview. If you can include an example term sheet range that shows the math for a sample week of 6x traffic, that would help procurement.

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Liao
Head of Platform, Acme Analytics

Attachment: Acme_Monthly_usage_preview.csv (CSV, 42KB)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liao <sarah.liao@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-08T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 event - temporary spike needs + Dedicated sizing question

Sarah — thanks for the detail and the CSV. High level answers up front:

- Recommended approach: keep your baseline reserved commit sized to cover 1.5x typical steady demand, then add a surge overlay ("elastic top-up") for predictable short periods. This minimizes long-term commit cost while keeping a bounded overlay spend.
- Surge pricing model we typically propose: a tiered per-GPU surge rate (hourly) with an incremental step after a soft cap. We enforce per-tenant cooldown windows to avoid thrash (default 15 min; adjustable). Billing granularity is per-minute after the first 5 minutes.
- Discount tradeoffs: adding a modest monthly reserved bump (~20% of peak) reduces overlay exposure and gives a 10–18% blended discount across committed units.

I'll run an example math on your CSV and get back with a proposed term sheet. Copying Monica and Marissa for capacity & pricing detail.

—Jordan
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-09T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Q4 event - temporary spike needs + Dedicated sizing question

Jordan — I pulled the CSV and modeled two concrete scenarios for Acme:

Scenario A (Conservative commit + overlay):
- Reserved commit: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (covers ~1.5x steady)
- Surge overlay: up to +40 GPUs for up to 168 hours (1 week)
- Surge cap: 40 GPUs; soft cap at +20 GPUs where lower surge rate applies
- Cooldown: 20 minutes default between scale events
- Pricing: $X/hour/GPU for reserved (committed), overlay base rate of $1.80/hour/GPU up to soft cap, $2.50/hour/GPU beyond soft cap
- Estimated blended monthly cost for October with spike: $YYk

Scenario B (Higher commit, smaller overlay):
- Reserved commit: 30 x A100-equivalent GPUs (covers ~peak minus a small overlay)
- Surge overlay: up to +10 GPUs for up to 72 hours
- Pricing: larger commit gives 22% discount on reserved unit price; overlay base rate drops to $1.10/hour/GPU until soft cap; beyond that $1.85/hour/GPU
- Estimated blended monthly cost for October with spike: $ZZk (lower peak overlay spend, higher baseline)

Notes: both scenarios assume per-minute billing after an initial 5-minute allocation. We can tweak cooldowns (shorten to 5 minutes for faster response but increases risk of oscillation) or implement an SLA-backed throughput guarantee on committed capacity at a premium.

I attached numbers in a Drive sheet; Jordan, can you review and share with Sarah?

—Monica
Principal Solutions Engineer
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liao <sarah.liao@acme-analytics.com>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-09T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 event - temporary spike needs + Dedicated sizing question

Sarah / Tom — attaching a concise term-sheet range with numbers mapped to Monica's scenarios and a short comparison table (reserved vs overlay cost, cooldowns, SLA options). Important callouts:
1) We can offer a temporary surge credit covering the first 48 hours of the event equal to 100 GPU-hours (applied as a one-time credit) if Acme signs a 6-month reserved commitment at the Scenario B level.
2) Cooldown tuning: we recommend a 10-minute default for this workload (balancing responsiveness and stability).
3) Surge rate cap: we propose a hard cap at +50 GPUs to protect other tenants; soft cap at +20 GPUs gets lower rates.

Attachment: redwood_proposed_term_sheet_v3.pdf (PDF, 88KB)

Next step: if this aligns, procurement can review and we can spin up a demo config in a sandbox for validation. Thoughts?

—Jordan
From: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme-analytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Sarah Liao <sarah.liao@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2026-10-10T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 event - temporary spike needs + Dedicated sizing question

Thanks — Jordan and team. A couple procurement questions before we loop legal: 1) can the 100 GPU-hour credit be applied as a rolling monthly credit if not used in the 48-hour window? 2) is the hard cap adjustable for enterprise customers (we may want higher but understand risk)? 3) what are the exact cooldown semantics — is it tenant-level or route-level?

Also curious if you can provide a short example that converts the overlay rates to $/1M tokens for our cost modeling (we primarily model against token throughput).

—Tom
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@acme-analytics.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, procurement@acme-analytics.com
Date: 2026-10-11T15:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 event - temporary spike needs + Dedicated sizing question

Tom — quick answers and clarifications: 1) Credit flexibility: we can make the 100 GPU-hour credit convert to a 6-month rolling credit pool if you sign the 6-month commit; unused capacity will auto-expire after the commitment term. We cannot make it open-ended for accounting reasons but can pro-rate on early termination.
2) Hard cap: adjustable for enterprise customers; anything above +80 GPUs requires a safety review and a temporary allocation process, but we can accommodate with a short notice window.
3) Cooldown semantics: tenant-level by default (all routes for the tenant observe the cooldown). We offer route-level tuning for customers that own multiple independent products under one tenant, but that requires additional routing config and a small setup fee.

As for $/1M tokens: using Acme's sample workload (avg tokens per request = 1.2k, avg GPU throughput = 1.5M tokens/hour per A100-equivalent), overlay rate of $1.80/hour/GPU maps to roughly $1.20 per 1M tokens at the soft-cap rate; beyond soft cap it's about $1.70 per 1M tokens. I'll add the exact formula to the Drive sheet.

If that looks good we'd propose: sign a 6-month Scenario B commit, onboard sandbox this week, and apply the rolling credit. I'll loop legal on a redline-ready term; Jordan, can you confirm procurement contact details so we can start the SOW?

—Marissa
VP, Dedicated Sales
Redwood Inference
